State of the search after W: split-band DRAM is near its true floor (KV read exactly once, partials at 16 bits - the width lever is spent without dropping below contract output precision, stage-depth/ns levers closed, combine latency and capture fill removed); the big band remains a register-wall structural optimum without tcgen05; the single-pass band is max-free with arithmetic efficiency partly spent. It is categorically distinct from both levers E5A1 declined when it did not start a Direction W: option (a) was barred because the mid band's stage1 has 'no second reducible mass' for ALU/overhead cuts (Section 21 law b: ALU cuts cannot pay on DRAM-bound bands) - W shrinks the saturated mass itself (partials traffic IS part of the 80.52% SOL bytes); Section 17's counter-case (traffic cuts gained only 4.8% of predicted) was the big band at dram 6.09%, not BW-bound, whereas split stage1 is at 80.52%. fp16 over bf16: 11-bit vs 8-bit mantissa keeps added error 8x below the output rounding already accepted. fp16 over fp8: no numeric headroom argument needed at 11 bits, and sm_120 DRAM bytes are dtype-agnostic for stores. findings.lesson: On a DRAM-saturated band every non-byte lever class can be closed (ALU, occupancy, latency, passes) while the byte-count lever stays open; dtype-narrowing an intermediate is the cheapest byte cut, and its measured magnitude must be discounted for L2 reuse of write-then-read windows.

findings.root_cause: On bands where stage1 sits at dram 80.52% SOL with traffic already minimal (L2:DRAM 1.06), time ~= bytes/BW, so halving the partials component (3-39% of split-call DRAM bytes) pays; the shortfall comes from L2 absorbing part of the short partials write->read-back window, which the naive model charged entirely to DRAM.

findings.lesson: For tolerance-class edits, derive the A/B added-error gate from the perturbation model and check which term of the evaluator criterion (atol vs rtol vs ULP) dominates the observed magnitude regime before setting the bar; gate revisions are legitimate only when derived and recorded before the rerun, never after seeing candidate verdicts.
findings.observation: Strict one-ULP A/B parity (gate rev #3) false-failed a provably-safe candidate: 516-17970 elements per cohort flagged with diff exactly 2^-11 = 4.9e-4 at near-zero |A| (ULP ratios up to 2^17) while evaluator violations were 0 and worst margins were IDENTICAL to the champion's; the flagged diffs are 4.9% of atol.
findings.resolution: Pre-registered gate revision #4 before the rerun: bound |arm-A| <= bf16_ULP(|A|) + GATE_SLACK*VMAX with GATE_SLACK = 2^-10 (2x the analytic 2^-11 fp16-RNE perturbation bound) PLUS margin parity (arm worst margin <= A's + 0.05). Run 5 passed with >= 11x typical headroom (bound_ratio_max <= 0.0914; 0.7529 worst = the legitimate 1-ULP bf16-flip class); pathology classes stay caught by orders of magnitude (fp16 lse -> ~0.07*O(1) >> bound). Trusted ABBA confirmed: error metrics identical to champion's on all 90 hidden shapes.
findings.root_cause: Near-zero outputs live in the ATOL-DOMINATED regime of the evaluator criterion (|x-ref| <= atol + rtol|x|): ulp(|A|) collapses toward 2^-28 while added fp16 rounding noise is ABSOLUTE (~2^-11 * VMAX, since out_s is a convex combination of bf16 v rows bounded by max|v|) - a pure ULP-ratio bar is magnitude-wrong there exactly as flat/relative bars were magnitude-wrong in the ULP regime (rev #2's failure).

findings.lesson: After any protocol rerun, VERIFY a fresh job_id before trusting the output; to force a fresh dev run of an unchanged script, perturb the request identity in a way the command semantics ignore (trailing argv token + distinct note).
findings.observation: The G2 protocol rerun (after run-1's tiny twin-floor breach) silently did not happen: re-firing the byte-identical dev request returned the SAME job_id (dv_9f4550113186) with byte-identical stdout instead of a fresh run.
findings.resolution: Changed request identity semantically-inertly: appended an argv token the probe ignores (dispatch is on argv[1] only) plus a distinct note (gateway enforces notes <= 200 chars; a longer note drew a 400) -> fresh job dv_42252b989253, ok=true. Deposited as knowledge Section 23 law (d).
findings.root_cause: gateway-execute dev operations dedupe on request identity like evaluate/profile - an identical request replays the recorded result. A rerun protocol that re-fires the same request therefore measures nothing new, and a naive agent could mistake the replay for a reproduced verdict.

findings.lesson: A dtype cut on a latency-bound post-kernel buys TWO effects - bytes and register pressure/occupancy - and on tiny graphs the second can dominate; band-level over/under-performance vs a single-mechanism model is diagnostic, not noise.
findings.observation: The tiny band OVER-performed its byte-model prediction: dev cohorts 1.146-1.153 vs predicted 1.02-1.08, and tiny was the best ABBA band (1.02109) despite the smallest partials fraction (~10% of stage1 bytes).
findings.resolution: No action needed (kept with the candidate); recorded as the fresh hint that small-grid post-kernels still respond to register-pressure cuts even after V's chain-shortening.
findings.root_cause: fp16 partial loads halved the combine kernel's register-resident data: regs 178-216 -> 166-168 raised occupancy 2 -> 3 CTAs/SM (measured at G1, free at <=512-CTA grids per Section 22 law a) - on ~27us latency-bound graphs that occupancy and latency relief adds on top of the pure byte cut.

hypothesis: Direction W: switching the packed split path's out_part partials from fp32 to fp16 (lse_part stays fp32) halves partials write (stage1) + read-back (combine/fused tail) DRAM bytes on the DRAM-saturated split bands (stage1 dram 80.52% SOL, L2:DRAM 1.06 on shape 58; partials are 3-39% of split-call bytes by cohort), predicting trusted ABBA pooled 1.02-1.05 with gains scaling by the partials fraction (small band largest, mid next, single-pass shapes exactly 1.000). Precision stays inside contract tolerance: fp16 adds <=2^-11 relative rounding on out_s (a convex combination of bf16 v rows, |out_s| <= VMAX, far below fp16 range), 8x finer than the accepted bf16 output rounding. MEASURED OUTCOME: direction confirmed (all three split bands gained, big band 0.99997 ~ 1.000 exactly, no wrong-way cohort), magnitude under the naive bytes/BW model (pooled 1.01173) - L2 absorbs part of the short partials write-to-read-back window; the byte model ranks and directs but does not price (knowledge Section 23 law b).

knowledge_used.application: Chose a byte-cut (not ALU-cut) lever for the saturated split bands; ran G0 CPU sim before any GPU spend; margin bar 0.5 adopted; dilution math set the keep bar (pooled >= 1.005 over 90 shapes with f = 68-70/90 split-dispatched).

profile_evidence.evidence_chain: Shape 58: dram 80.52% SOL + L2:DRAM 1.06 => stage1 time ~= bytes/BW and traffic is already minimal => the only lever is shrinking bytes => partials (fp32 write + fp32 read-back = 2x batch*mq_pad*heads*S*256*4B) are 3-39% of split-call DRAM bytes => fp16 halves that component => predicted per-cohort gains follow the byte-fraction ordering (smallpf > small > mid > fused). Shape 72: dram 6.09% => big band is traffic-immune => predicted exactly ~1.000 as an untouched control. MEASURED confirmation: ABBA bands tiny 1.02109 / small 1.01873 / mid 1.01223 all gained, big 0.99997 ~ 1.000 exactly, no cohort wrong-way; magnitude under the naive model because the profiles' L2:DRAM 1.06 also implies the short partials write->read-back window is partly L2-served (Section 23 law b, L2 discount).
profile_evidence.evidence_summary: Reused trusted SOL profiles of the champion lineage from the Direction P audit (experiment_1f3b73fddc5347b9b23d7480cb14eab9, profile trial gtrial_31cb8f288a2e59e10e7adc9b697e92a7, both completed). Shape 58 (mid band, 150-1000us): _split_kv_stage1_packed = 263.840us = 95.14% of the 277.312us call, bound MEMORY with dram throughput 80.52% of roofline (1031.98 GB/s achieved), occupancy 8.33% (1 CTA/SM), dram_bytes_read 262.88MB vs l2_bytes 279.53MB = ratio 1.06 - NO reuse, every KV byte read from DRAM exactly once; _split_kv_combine 4.28% of the call reading 11.06MB. Shape 72 (big band, >1000us): single-pass kernel 100% of call, bound COMPUTE (54.51% vs memory 49.74%), dram only 6.09% - traffic-immune. No new profile was needed this attempt: the W hypothesis is a byte-count cut on the mass these profiles proved DRAM-saturated.
